title: Flatness and reduction data for the finite constant completion tower
statement: theorem finiteSystem_properties (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) : letI : ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Cᵒᵖ), Module (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)) (adicTerm J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) n U) := finiteSystemModule J A I; (∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Cᵒᵖ), IsScalarTower A (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)) (adicTerm J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) n U)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Cᵒᵖ), Module.Flat (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)) (adicTerm J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) n U)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Cᵒᵖ), Function.Surjective (adicTransition J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) (n + 1) n (Nat.le_succ n) U)) ∧ (∀ (m n : ℕ) (U : Cᵒᵖ), ∃ e : TensorProduct A (adicTerm J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) m U) (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)) ≃ₗ[A] adicTerm J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) (min m n) U, ∀ (b : adicTerm J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) m U) (a : A), e (b ⊗ₜ[A] Ideal.Quotient.mk _ a) = a • adicTransition J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) m (min m n) (Nat.min_le_left m n) U b)

proof.text: Install the canonical quotient-section module structures finiteSystemModule (defined in this module from the sheafification unit of the constant quotient presheaf). Prove the scalar tower directly from naturality of the sheafification unit. Apply the strictly smaller flatness-and-reduction theorem to obtain flatness and tensor reduction. Prove transition surjectivity by splitting the surjective quotient ring map on underlying types and transporting the sectionwise splitting through constant sheafification.
